posts.label: Morning AI update
posts.hook: AI changed again. Here is the bit a local business should care about.
posts.subhead: Use the news only if it changes how you reply, quote, create, book, or follow up.
slides: Why it matters for a Gold Coast small business.
One practical thing to test before lunch.
DM AUDIT if you want me to map yours.
posts.caption: Most AI news is noise. The useful question is simple: does this help you reply faster, quote faster, create faster, or follow up better? If yes, test it. If no, ignore it. DM AUDIT and I will tell you the first 3 tasks I would look at in your business.

posts.label: Offer
posts.hook: Four lessons. One practical AI setup for your business.
posts.subhead: Website, app, socials, loops. $1,000 for four in-person sessions on the Gold Coast.
slides: Session 1: connect to AI and build your website.
Session 2: turn the website into an app.
Session 3: connect your app to socials.
posts.caption: This is the simple local package: 4 in-person sessions at $250/hour. Session 1, connect to your AI and build your first website. Session 2, turn it into an app-style tool. Session 3, connect it to your socials. Session 4, run the content, lead, follow-up, review loop. DM COACH.

posts.label: Morning AI update
posts.hook: The AI update only matters if it saves a real job.
posts.subhead: Today look at quoting, booking, invoices, FAQs, and follow-up messages.
slides: Translate it into one business task.
Test it on old emails, old quotes, or old FAQs.
Keep the result if it saves time without making you sound weird.
posts.caption: The best AI test is not fancy. Take one repeated task you already do and see if the tool saves 15 minutes without dropping quality. That is the start of a real system.

posts.label: Evidence
posts.hook: A missed enquiry is not just one message.
posts.subhead: It is the quote you did not send, the follow-up you forgot, and the job that went to someone faster.
posts.caption: Small businesses do not usually need complicated AI first. They need fewer dropped leads. A simple enquiry and follow-up system can pay for itself faster than another content calendar.

posts.label: Morning AI update
posts.hook: AI search is changing how people find local businesses.
posts.subhead: Your website needs clear services, prices, location, proof, and next steps.
slides: People are asking AI before they click websites.
Your site should answer the sale, not just look nice.
posts.caption: If someone asks an AI tool for a local recommendation, vague websites lose. Make your service, suburb, price range, proof, and next step obvious.

posts.label: Education
posts.hook: AI will not fix a messy process.
posts.subhead: First we map the work. Then we automate the part that repeats.
slides: Where does the enquiry come from?
posts.caption: The first win is usually not a chatbot. It is a clear process. Once the process is clear, the automation gets simple.

posts.label: Morning AI update
posts.hook: New AI content tools are useful, but only with a repeatable angle.
posts.subhead: Do not post random AI images. Turn your real work into weekly proof, tips, and offers.
slides: Let AI draft, then edit for your voice.
Post the thing that sells the next step.
posts.caption: Content automation should not make your brand weirder. It should help you say the useful thing more consistently.

posts.label: Build offer
posts.hook: Need a client app, internal tool, or program builder?
posts.subhead: Custom builds start from $2,500. Good for portals, check-ins, dashboards, forms, and repeatable programs.
posts.caption: Some businesses do not need another SaaS subscription. They need one custom tool that fits the way they work. Custom app and program builds start from $2,500. DM BUILD.

posts.label: Morning AI update
posts.hook: Your inbox is probably the easiest AI win.
posts.subhead: Not auto-spam. Drafts, summaries, follow-up reminders, and cleaner handovers.
posts.caption: The goal is not to let AI run wild in your inbox. The goal is to stop good leads and client requests getting buried.

posts.label: CTA
posts.hook: I am taking on 5 Gold Coast businesses for AI audits.
posts.subhead: I will find the first 3 tasks worth automating before you spend money building anything.
slides: Good fit: forms, sheets, or client programs.
posts.caption: If you are curious but not sure what to build, start with the audit. I will look for the highest-value repeated work first. DM AUDIT.

posts.label: Weekend AI test
posts.hook: Weekend AI test: write your FAQ from real customer questions.
posts.subhead: Grab old enquiries, paste the themes, and turn them into clearer website answers.
slides: Put the best ones on your site.
Use them in DMs and emails.
posts.caption: A good FAQ is not filler. It shortens the sale because it answers the questions people ask before they trust you.

posts.label: Build proof
posts.hook: I build real systems, not AI slide decks.
posts.subhead: Apps, dashboards, content engines, lead workflows, and follow-up systems that have to survive real business use.
posts.caption: The useful version of AI is boring in the best way: fewer missed tasks, faster replies, clearer handovers, and tools people actually use.

posts.label: Sunday setup
posts.hook: Before Monday, pick one repeat task to remove.
posts.subhead: Do not overhaul the business. Choose the one thing you hate doing twice.
slides: That is enough for a first automation.
posts.caption: The best first automation is usually small. Pick one task that happens every week and make it easier before chasing the big shiny build.

posts.label: Checklist
posts.subhead: One inbox rule, one FAQ answer, one follow-up reminder, one content prompt, one owner approval step.
posts.caption: You do not need to become an AI expert next week. You just need one less manual task and one cleaner system.
